In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Franklin graph''' is a 3-[[regular graph|regular]] [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] with 12 vertices and 18 edges.

The Franklin graph is named after [[Philip Franklin]], who disproved the [[Heawood conjecture]] on the number of colors needed when a two-dimensional surface is partitioned into cells by a [[graph embedding]].<ref>Franklin, P. "A Six Color Problem." J. Math. Phys. 13, 363-379, 1934. {{doi|10.1002/sapm1934131363}}</ref> The Heawood conjecture implied that the maximum chromatic number of a map on the [[Klein bottle]] should be seven, but Franklin proved that in this case six colors always suffice. (The Klein bottle is the only surface for which the Heawood conjecture fails.) The Franklin graph can be embedded in the Klein bottle so that it forms a map requiring six colors, showing that six colors are sometimes necessary in this case. This embedding is the [[Petrie dual]] of its embedding in the [[projective plane]] shown below.

It is [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]] and has [[chromatic number]] 2, [[chromatic index]] 3, [[radius (graph theory)|radius]] 3, [[diameter (graph theory)|diameter]] 3 and [[girth (graph theory)|girth]] 4. It is also a 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]] [[perfect graph]].

==Algebraic properties==
The [[automorphism group]] of the Franklin graph is of [[order (group theory)|order]] 48 and is [[group isomorphism|isomorphic]] to '''Z'''/2'''Z'''×''S''<sub>4</sub>, the [[direct product of groups|direct product]] of the [[cyclic group]] '''Z'''/2'''Z''' and the [[symmetric group]] ''S''<sub>4</sub>. It [[group action|acts]] transitively on the vertices of the graph, making it [[vertex-transitive graph|vertex-transitive]].

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of the Franklin graph is
:<math>(x-3) (x-1)^3 (x+1)^3 (x+3) (x^2-3)^2.\ </math>
